paper.title_en: Effect of qubit's motion on quantum steering in leaky cavities
paper.abstract_en: Many strategies have been proposed to manipulate and protect symmetric quantum correlations against decoherence. However, more research is needed to focus on asymmetric correlations, such as quantum steering. To address this gap, we investigate the dynamics of quantum steering between two moving qubits within separate cavities. Specifically, we explore how the qubits' velocity impacts the dynamics of quantum steering. The results indicate that when each qubit interacts independently with its cavity, increasing its velocity can enhance quantum steering, regardless of whether the dynamics is Markovian or non-Markovian. We also find that the qubits' motion can effectively control the asymmetric nature of steering even when symmetric environmental noise acts on an initially asymmetric mixed state. Furthermore, we analyze the asymmetric properties of quantum steering by considering a scenario in which one qubit remains stationary in its cavity. The findings show that adjusting the velocity of the moving qubit can efficiently manipulate asymmetric properties, such as "one-way" and "two-way" steering, thereby enhancing quantum steering and manipulating its asymmetry without consuming external quantum resources in the cavities.
